correctness.rationale: The theorem is proved for all 496 two-site deletions. The dual Platonic codes each have covering cosine u; nonincident mixed deletions are protected by their cap-separation inequality v<2u^2-1. Same-class deletions leave one entire u-covering orbit. By incidence transitivity it suffices to compute a representative damaged convex hull. The 51 inherited triangles and exactly three new supporting polygons have a certified closed connected 54-face boundary; the unique nearest plane has Gram-distance gamma, strictly below u, beta and the original facet distance h. Unique deepest direction follows. The embedded standard-library checker independently verifies every strict support test using exact rational enclosing intervals and verifies the 54-face boundary, all combinatorial counts and closed radicals. Zero coplanar identities are separately proved by golden-ratio coordinate relations.

value.rationale: Two-point deletion robustness is a motivated geometric invariant of the unique 32-vertex volume-maximizing spherical configuration. The classification covers every possible pair and exhibits a strict incidence-controlled two-level phase: only 60 of 496 failures worsen the radius beyond the common baseline; in all of those failures there is exactly one deepest hole. This is not an arbitrary slice or a numerically guessed table, and the exceptional constant comes from a new quadrilateral supporting face unavailable in the intact polyhedron. The result separates coverage resilience from previously known volume-loss classes without asserting a global design optimum.
